gene_symbol: phaZ

  label: Pseudomonas putida KT2440
description: 'PhaZ (PP_5004) is the intracellular medium-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoate depolymerase
  of Pseudomonas putida KT2440. It hydrolyzes stored polyester and is inferred to act at PHA granules
  from close-strain KT2442 biochemical and localization experiments, corroborated by native KT2440 carbonosome-fraction
  detection. Its contribution to net storage depends on conditions: deletion did not improve PHA titre
  or yield in a tested p-coumarate accumulation regime. The KT2442 enzyme also exhibits weak secondary
  tributyrin hydrolysis, distinct from its principal polyester-mobilization role.'
existing_annotations:
- term:
    id: GO:0004806
    label: triacylglycerol lipase activity
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000118
  qualifier: enables
  review:
    summary: Very weak tributyrin hydrolysis is measured, but a biological secondary lipase function is
      unestablished.
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: PMID17170116 Table4 detects very low overnight tributyrin hydrolysis by purified KT2442 PhaZ;
      the assay is positive and GO0004806 does not exclude C4 triacylglycerol. However, physiological
      use and a meaningful secondary-function efficiency are not established. Under the repository enzyme-specificity
      policy this is the measured-activity/relevance-unknown tier, not sufficient support for KEEP_AS_NON_CORE.
      This does not deny the chemistry, assign native KT2440 glycerolipid catabolism, or infer absolute
      inability to hydrolyze triacylglycerols. The KT2442-to-KT2440 transfer remains qualified.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:analysis/module_audits/bacterial_mcl_pha_synthesis_and_mobilization/psepk-consultation/primary-scope.md
      supporting_text: 'Table 4 reports tributyrin hydrolysis: “A very low but detectable activity was
        observed when the assay was developed overnight.”'
- term:
    id: GO:0046503
    label: glycerolipid catabolic process
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000118
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: The established native role is PHA turnover; a physiological glycerolipid-catabolic assignment
      is not demonstrated.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: Polyester hydrolysis is not glycerol-backbone lipid breakdown. Although low tributyrin hydrolysis
      is a real secondary molecular activity of the KT2442 enzyme, that in-vitro activity does not establish
      native glycerolipid catabolism. Retain the supported process interpretation by lateral replacement
      with GO:0042620, using close-strain biochemistry and native KT2440 locus/perturbation context; no
      universal knockout benefit is claimed.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0042620
      label: poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) metabolic process
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:17170116
      supporting_text: We have demonstrated that PhaZ is an intracellular depolymerase that is located
        in PHA granules and that hydrolyzes specifically mcl-PHAs containing aliphatic and aromatic monomers.
    - reference_id: PMID:31468725
      supporting_text: Although the deletion of phaZ did not improve titres or yields
- term:
    id: GO:0070088
    label: polyhydroxyalkanoate granule
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:17170116
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: Historical target-direct granule proposal retired for strain/provenance precision, not rejection
      of localization.
    action: NEW
    reason: The retained historical payload assigns IDA/PMID17170116 to KT2440 Q88D24, but that paper
      directly assays KT2442-derived PhaZ and KT2442 granule fractions. No complete construct-to-target
      sequence bridge was established. Retire this proposal in place; preserve every source field and
      action NEW. Granule localization remains a qualified core inference supported by KT2442 immunoblot
      and native KT2440 fraction detection in PMID38608840 (7 unique peptides,20.1% coverage; no enrichment/bona-fide
      marker). No replacement NEW is introduced.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:analysis/module_audits/bacterial_mcl_pha_synthesis_and_mobilization/psepk-consultation/primary-scope.md
      supporting_text: Fig. 7 immunoblot localizes PhaZ to KT2442 granule fractions.
    - reference_id: file:analysis/module_audits/bacterial_mcl_pha_synthesis_and_mobilization/psepk-consultation/primary-scope.md
      supporting_text: GranuleEnrich and bona-fide markers are blank for all three.
    source_defects:
    - defect_type: WRONG_EVIDENCE_CODE
      resource: OTHER
      record: Historical repository-authored Q88D24/GO:0070088 proposal
      slot: evidence_type
      asserted_value: IDA
      confidence: CONFIRMED
      explanation: 'The historical repository proposal overstates direct target-strain provenance: PMID17170116
        experimentally localizes KT2442 PhaZ, not native KT2440 Q88D24. Retired in place, without denying
        localization or changing the original payload.'
  retired: true

  findings: []

  title: 'Biochemical evidence that phaZ gene encodes a specific intracellular medium chain length polyhydroxyalkanoate
    depolymerase in Pseudomonas putida KT2442: characterization of a paradigmatic enzyme.'
  findings:
  - statement: KT2442 PhaZ was purified after E. coli expression; granule association and hydrolysis are

    supporting_text: We have demonstrated that PhaZ is an intracellular depolymerase that is located in

document.description: PhaZ (PP_5004) is the intracellular medium-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoate depolymerase of Pseudomonas putida KT2440. It hydrolyzes stored polyester and is inferred to act at PHA granules from close-strain KT2442 biochemical and localization experiments, corroborated by native KT2440 carbonosome-fraction detection. Its contribution to net storage depends on conditions: deletion did not improve PHA titre or yield in a tested p-coumarate accumulation regime. The KT2442 enzyme also exhibits weak secondary tributyrin hydrolysis, distinct from its principal polyester-mobilization role.

review.summary: Very weak tributyrin hydrolysis is measured, but a biological secondary lipase function is unestablished.
review.reason: PMID17170116 Table4 detects very low overnight tributyrin hydrolysis by purified KT2442 PhaZ; the assay is positive and GO0004806 does not exclude C4 triacylglycerol. However, physiological use and a meaningful secondary-function efficiency are not established. Under the repository enzyme-specificity policy this is the measured-activity/relevance-unknown tier, not sufficient support for KEEP_AS_NON_CORE. This does not deny the chemistry, assign native KT2440 glycerolipid catabolism, or infer absolute inability to hydrolyze triacylglycerols. The KT2442-to-KT2440 transfer remains qualified.

supported_by.supporting_text: Table 4 reports tributyrin hydrolysis: “A very low but detectable activity was observed when the assay was developed overnight.”

review.summary: The established native role is PHA turnover; a physiological glycerolipid-catabolic assignment is not demonstrated.

summary: Alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold (AB hydrolase-1) proteins. SF5 holds the gammaproteobacterial biotin
  pathway esterase BioH (pimeloyl-ACP methyl ester esterase, E. coli P13001) and the Pseudomonas 3-hydroxyacyl
  transacylases PhaG and RhlA. SF3 holds the B. subtilis stress-signalling protein RsbQ. SF2 holds yeast
  Lpx1 and diverse bacterial and eukaryotic hydrolases (RutD-like carbamate hydrolases, Rv0045c, RufB).

  hydrolase-1 domain; it adds an N-terminal lipoyl domain. PhaG forward ACP-to-CoA routing is favored
  by heterologous metabolic controls; purified reverse CoA-to-ACP transfer is measured, while forward
  acyl-ACP kinetics remain unmeasured in the cited studies.

  BioH ester hydrolysis in biotin synthesis, PhaG/RhlA acyl transfer, RsbQ signaling, and Lpx1 lipase
  activity. Fold membership does not establish a specific substrate or uniform hydrolysis. The lipoyl-domain
  acetoin E2s remain grouped by NCBIfam NF011457, not this family.'

document.summary: Alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold (AB hydrolase-1) proteins. SF5 holds the gammaproteobacterial biotin pathway esterase BioH (pimeloyl-ACP methyl ester esterase, E. coli P13001) and the Pseudomonas 3-hydroxyacyl transacylases PhaG and RhlA. SF3 holds the B. subtilis stress-signalling protein RsbQ. SF2 holds yeast Lpx1 and diverse bacterial and eukaryotic hydrolases (RutD-like carbamate hydrolases, Rv0045c, RufB). The P. putida KT2440 acetoin-system E2 AcoC (Q88QE1) is classified in SF2 through its C-terminal AB hydrolase-1 domain; it adds an N-terminal lipoyl domain. PhaG forward ACP-to-CoA routing is favored by heterologous metabolic controls; purified reverse CoA-to-ACP transfer is measured, while forward acyl-ACP kinetics remain unmeasured in the cited studies.
document.coherence_reason: Members share an alpha/beta-hydrolase fold but have different established chemistries: BioH ester hydrolysis in biotin synthesis, PhaG/RhlA acyl transfer, RsbQ signaling, and Lpx1 lipase activity. Fold membership does not establish a specific substrate or uniform hydrolysis. The lipoyl-domain acetoin E2s remain grouped by NCBIfam NF011457, not this family.

preferred_name: ABHD6-type monoacylglycerol lipases and related alpha/beta hydrolases
summary: An alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold family named for vertebrate ABHD6, a membrane-anchored monoacylglycerol
  lipase that also associates with AMPA-type glutamate receptors (SF5). Most other members are uncharacterized
  bacterial, fungal, algal and plant AB hydrolases (SF31, SF33, SF26 and others). The Pseudomonas putida
  PpG2 acetoin-system E2 AcoC (Q59695) and the P. putida KT2440 NicD protein are classified in SF33 through
  their C-terminal AB hydrolase-1 domain. AcoC adds an N-terminal lipoyl domain and is assigned as a dihydrolipoyllysine-residue
  acetyltransferase. The same SF5 also contains the bacterial intracellular-PHA-mobilization protein PhaZ
  P26495 from Ectopseudomonas oleovorans GPo1; the ABHD6 subfamily label does not establish monoacylglycerol
  specificity for that member.
functional_coherence: HETEROGENEOUS
coherence_reason: 'The alpha/beta-hydrolase fold is shared, but experimentally supported activities are
  few and clade-specific: monoacylglycerol lipase for ABHD6 (SF5), and epoxide hydrolase or uracil catabolism
  for single bacterial seeds. SF33 is a mixture of fungal and algal putative hydrolases plus the lipoyl-domain
  AcoC. Membrane and lipase assertions seeded by ABHD6 do not hold for the soluble E2 AcoC. The proteobacterial
  lipoyl/AB-hydrolase acetoin E2s are grouped by NCBIfam NF011457 rather than by any one PANTHER family.
  GPo1 PhaZ adds a directly supported native polyester-mobilization role within SF5. The reviewed ABHD6
  positive remains valid; a new PhaZ function does not prove loss of possible secondary monoacylglycerol
  hydrolysis.'

document.preferred_name: ABHD6-type monoacylglycerol lipases and related alpha/beta hydrolases
document.summary: An alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold family named for vertebrate ABHD6, a membrane-anchored monoacylglycerol lipase that also associates with AMPA-type glutamate receptors (SF5). Most other members are uncharacterized bacterial, fungal, algal and plant AB hydrolases (SF31, SF33, SF26 and others). The Pseudomonas putida PpG2 acetoin-system E2 AcoC (Q59695) and the P. putida KT2440 NicD protein are classified in SF33 through their C-terminal AB hydrolase-1 domain. AcoC adds an N-terminal lipoyl domain and is assigned as a dihydrolipoyllysine-residue acetyltransferase. The same SF5 also contains the bacterial intracellular-PHA-mobilization protein PhaZ P26495 from Ectopseudomonas oleovorans GPo1; the ABHD6 subfamily label does not establish monoacylglycerol specificity for that member.
document.coherence_reason: The alpha/beta-hydrolase fold is shared, but experimentally supported activities are few and clade-specific: monoacylglycerol lipase for ABHD6 (SF5), and epoxide hydrolase or uracil catabolism for single bacterial seeds. SF33 is a mixture of fungal and algal putative hydrolases plus the lipoyl-domain AcoC. Membrane and lipase assertions seeded by ABHD6 do not hold for the soluble E2 AcoC. The proteobacterial lipoyl/AB-hydrolase acetoin E2s are grouped by NCBIfam NF011457 rather than by any one PANTHER family. GPo1 PhaZ adds a directly supported native polyester-mobilization role within SF5. The reviewed ABHD6 positive remains valid; a new PhaZ function does not prove loss of possible secondary monoacylglycerol hydrolysis.

id: MODULE:bacterial_mcl_pha_synthesis_and_mobilization
title: Bacterial medium-chain-length PHA synthesis and intracellular mobilization
description: Intracellular storage-polyester synthesis and turnover begin with a supplied pool of medium-chain
  (R)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA. Substrate-compatible PhaC enzymes polymerize hydroxyacyl units, and intracellular
  PhaZ enzymes mobilize the resulting storage polymer. PhaG-dependent transfer from fatty-acid-synthesis
  intermediates provides an optional upstream supply route. Polymer composition, synthase substrate acceptance
  and depolymerase access depend on the enzyme, substrate pool and native granule context.

  title: A new metabolic link between fatty acid de novo synthesis and polyhydroxyalkanoic acid synthesis.
    The PHAG gene from Pseudomonas putida KT2440 encodes a 3-hydroxyacyl-acyl carrier protein-coenzyme
    a transferase.
  statement: Native PhaG-linked routing and heterologous complementation connect fatty-acid synthesis
    to PHA production. Purified-transfer evidence is interpreted with the measured reaction direction;
    the 2022 forward-routing controls qualify the earlier chemistry debate.

document.title: Bacterial medium-chain-length PHA synthesis and intracellular mobilization
document.description: Intracellular storage-polyester synthesis and turnover begin with a supplied pool of medium-chain (R)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA. Substrate-compatible PhaC enzymes polymerize hydroxyacyl units, and intracellular PhaZ enzymes mobilize the resulting storage polymer. PhaG-dependent transfer from fatty-acid-synthesis intermediates provides an optional upstream supply route. Polymer composition, synthase substrate acceptance and depolymerase access depend on the enzyme, substrate pool and native granule context.

evidence.title: A new metabolic link between fatty acid de novo synthesis and polyhydroxyalkanoic acid synthesis. The PHAG gene from Pseudomonas putida KT2440 encodes a 3-hydroxyacyl-acyl carrier protein-coenzyme a transferase.
evidence.statement: Native PhaG-linked routing and heterologous complementation connect fatty-acid synthesis to PHA production. Purified-transfer evidence is interpreted with the measured reaction direction; the 2022 forward-routing controls qualify the earlier chemistry debate.

evidence.title: Metabolic engineering and characterization of phaC1 and phaC2 genes from Pseudomonas putida KCTC1639 for overproduction of medium-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoate.
evidence.statement: KCTC1639 overexpression supports condition-dependent synthase differences in that strain; it does not establish a sequential PhaC1/PhaC2 pathway or the same division of labor in KT2440.

evidence.title: Influence of growth stage on activities of polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) polymerase and PHA depolymerase in Pseudomonas putida U.
evidence.statement: P. putida U growth-stage studies support simultaneous polymerization and depolymerization; their kinetics are not relabeled as KT2440 or GPo1 measurements.

evidence.title: Biochemical evidence that phaZ gene encodes a specific intracellular medium chain length polyhydroxyalkanoate depolymerase in Pseudomonas putida KT2442: characterization of a paradigmatic enzyme.
evidence.statement: Characterizes intracellular KT2442 PhaZ on medium-chain PHA. Applying intrinsic activity to the KT2440 reference is a close-strain inference, not a native KT2440 assay; no complete sequence equality is asserted. Weak secondary tributyrin hydrolysis is distinct from native glycerolipid flux.

evidence.title: Current trends in medium-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoates: Microbial production, purification, and characterization.
evidence.statement: The mcl range is C6–C14, distinct from C3–C5 scl-PHA. Wild-type production reports extend beyond Pseudomonas, but a polymer-production report does not identify the matching synthase/depolymerase pair or license family-only role transfer. Composition depends on feedstock; C8/C10 are frequent, not exclusive.

evidence.title: Polyhydroxyalkanoate-associated phasins as phylogenetically heterogeneous, multipurpose proteins.
evidence.statement: Phasins organize granules and influence accumulation, segregation and enzyme access. These are adjacent granule functions, not additional obligatory chemical reactions in the bounded synthase-plus-intracellular-depolymerase profile; PHB-specific phasin dependencies cannot automatically be transferred to mcl systems.

evidence.title: Metabolic engineering strategies to produce medium-chain oleochemicals via acyl-ACP:CoA transacylase activity.
evidence.statement: KT2440 PhaG expressed in E. coli supports forward ACP-to-CoA routing in genetic product-sink comparisons: the product does not depend on FadD reactivation. The paper explicitly lacks direct forward acyl-ACP in-vitro kinetics. Endogenous thioesterases offer an alternative explanation for free hydroxyacids in older experiments. The main subsequent enzyme optimization uses P. koreensis PhaG and is not KT2440 native physiology.

evidence.title: Biochemical characterization of the Pseudomonas putida 3-hydroxyacyl ACP:CoA transacylase, which diverts intermediates of fatty acid de novo biosynthesis.
evidence.statement: Purified/refolded P. putida PhaG was measured transferring hydroxyacyl groups from CoA to ACP: direct reverse-reaction evidence, not a direct forward-ACP assay. Abstract also reports cytosolic localization and substrate-dependent dimerization. Exact target strain/construct requires fuller source bridge.

evidence.title: Development of a new strategy for production of medium-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoates by recombinant Escherichia coli via inexpensive non-fatty acid feedstocks.
evidence.statement: This study inferred PhaG thioesterase chemistry from heterologous free hydroxyacid accumulation and increased PHA when PP0763 was coexpressed. It did not isolate PhaG hydrolysis from endogenous CoA-thioester hydrolysis. Preserve the observed phenotype while reassessing that interpretation against the 2022 controls; do not make PP0763 universally required for PhaG routing. Native KT2440 polymer composition is measured separately from recombinant E. coli output.

evidence.title: Metabolism of poly(3-hydroxyalkanoates) (PHAs) by Pseudomonas oleovorans. Identification and sequences of genes and function of the encoded proteins in the synthesis and degradation of PHA.
evidence.statement: The original GPo1 locus study selected synthase/degradation complementation and sequenced the two synthases and intervening depolymerase. M58445 CDS translations exactly match P26494/P26495/P26496. It does not establish a mandatory sequential C1/C2 division, and the abstract reports no clear specificity difference.

evidence.title: Polyhydroxyalkanoate degradation is associated with nucleotide accumulation and enhances stress resistance and survival of Pseudomonas oleovorans in natural water microcosms.
evidence.statement: Native GPo1 and GPo500 phaZ were compared for polymer mobilization, with genetic complementation. The rescuing construct contains phaC1 plus phaZ and their promoter, so it is not purified single-protein reconstitution. The mutant is leaky, not absolute zero turnover. ATP/ppGpp and survival are consequences, not additional PhaZ catalytic functions. The source describes primarily C8/C6 polymer.

evidence.title: The Pseudomonas aeruginosa phaG gene product is involved in the synthesis of polyhydroxyalkanoic acid consisting of medium-chain-length constituents from non-related carbon sources.
evidence.statement: PAO1 PhaG supports complementation of a P. putida phaG mutant; the resulting polymer contains C6/C8/C10/C12. Native P. aeruginosa phaG disruption reduces gluconate-supported PHA to about 40% of wild type while fatty-acid-supported accumulation remains at wild-type level. This establishes a useful, nonobligatory substrate-routing role, not direct purified target chemistry. AF209711 exactly matches Q51553.

evidence.title: In vitro synthesis of poly(3-hydroxydecanoate): purification and enzymatic characterization of type II polyhydroxyalkanoate synthases PhaC1 and PhaC2 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
evidence.statement: Purified His-tagged P. aeruginosa class II PhaC1/PhaC2 synthesize poly(3-hydroxydecanoate) in vitro. Exact modern PAO1 PhaC1 construct identity remains unresolved: historical X66592 C1 is 557 aa versus current 559 aa. C2 and depolymerase archive sequences match modern entries, but adding a full PAO1 panel is unnecessary for the present mechanism comparison.

evidence.title: Revealing the essential role of the lid in mclPHA intracellular depolymerase from Pseudomonas putida KT2440.
evidence.statement: Despite KT2440 in its title, the assayed pPAZ3/template derives from KT2442 and protein is expressed in E. coli. GPo1 supplies radiolabeled polymer, not the enzyme. WT PhaZ acts on mcl polymer and pNP ester substrates; commercial polymer is mainly C8 with C6. Do not transfer native KT2440 localization, whole-strain phenotypes or variant kinetics from this paper without identity/context qualification. Extracellular GK13 comparator is a distinct compartmental role.

evidence.title: Analysis of in vivo substrate specificity of the PHA synthase from Ralstonia eutropha: formation of novel copolyesters in recombinant Escherichia coli.
evidence.statement: The Ralstonia eutropha class I PhaC produces 3HB/3HO and 3HB/3HO/3HDD copolyesters in engineered E. coli. This supports medium-chain comonomer acceptance, not pure or predominantly medium-chain polymer or complete native intracellular turnover. The primary abstract distinguishes this single-synthase result from the separate two-synthase blend control; exact assay-construct sequence equality remains unverified.

evidence.title: High amounts of medium-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoates subunits can be accumulated in recombinant Cupriavidus necator with wild-type synthase.
evidence.statement: Cupriavidus necator H16 with its unmodified native synthase accumulates SCL–MCL copolymer after engineered precursor routing. Class I membership therefore cannot exclude medium-chain incorporation. This engineered substrate-pool result does not establish complete native MCL synthesis and mobilization or a matched depolymerase.

document.notes: The core boundary starts at externally supplied hydroxyacyl-CoA and includes polymerization plus intracellular mobilization; requiring PhaZ for this combined profile does not make it necessary for synthesis alone. KT2440 and exact GPo1 references anchor the core; PAO1 PhaG is an optional-route comparator, not a complete separately reviewed PAO1 panel. GPo1 taxonomy/nomenclature aliases denote one strain. The unverified Q9KJH8 sequence-only PhaG representative is not retained as an equally direct functional exemplar. Class II PhaCs are positive anchors rather than a universal exclusion of class I medium-chain acceptance. PhaZ family placements 43433 and 43798 remain distinct with source-qualified substrate/function evidence. A KT2440 historical direct-localization proposal is retired in place solely for unsupported target-direct provenance, while qualified core localization is retained. Provider artifacts remain immutable discovery inputs; current primary evidence determines the mechanism. Full validation, capacity closure and independent review remain pending. CUPNH/phaC P23608 is reviewed as a class I substrate-range comparator. Its supported SCL–MCL copolymer incorporation is distinct from the matched synthase/depolymerase core panels.

# phaZ Gene Review Notes

## Identifier Mapping

- In KT2440, the literature gene name `phaZ` maps to locus `PP_5004` and UniProt `Q88D24`, even though the UniProt gene line currently says `Name=phaB`. [file:PSEPK/phaZ/phaZ-uniprot.txt, "SubName: Full=Poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) depolymerase"; "GN   Name=phaB"; "GN   OrderedLocusNames=PP_5004"; "DR   ESTHER; psepu-PHAZ; PHA_depolymerase_arom."]

## Core Function

- PhaZ is the intracellular granule-associated depolymerase that mobilizes stored medium-chain-length PHA in KT2440. [JBC 2007 PDF, "first formal biochemical evidence that PhaZ is certainly an intracellular mcl-PHA depolymerase"; https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/ae3e/1d24baa56e7222a02f12b2b3b75ee84cee02.pdf]
- Biochemical work on the highly similar KT2442 ortholog showed that 3-hydroxyoctanoate monomer is the main hydrolysis product and classified PhaZ as an endo/exo-mcl-PHA depolymerase. [JBC 2007 PDF, "the monomer of HO was identified as the main product of PhaZ hydrolysis"; "classify PhaZ as an endo/exo-mcl-PHA depolymerase"; https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/ae3e/1d24baa56e7222a02f12b2b3b75ee84cee02.pdf]
- The best current molecular-function term is GO:0050527 poly(3-hydroxyoctanoate) depolymerase activity rather than triacylglycerol lipase activity. [AmiGO GO:0050527, "poly(3-hydroxyoctanoate) depolymerase activity"; https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0050527]

## Physiological Role

- Deletion of phaZ increases and stabilizes PHA accumulation, showing that PP_5004 participates in poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) metabolic process in vivo. [PMC3918157, "the Delta phaZ knockout phenotype suggests that the PhaZ depolymerase is a major determinant of PHA accumulation and maintenance in the cell"; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3918157/]
- PhaZ is associated with polyhydroxyalkanoate granules rather than glycerolipid catabolism. [JBC 2007 PDF, "Identification of PhaZ as granule-associated protein"; PMC6922519, "the gene encoding the PHA depolymerase (phaZ; PP_5004) was deleted"; https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/ae3e/1d24baa56e7222a02f12b2b3b75ee84cee02.pdf; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6922519/]

## GO Review Implications

- GO:0004806 triacylglycerol lipase activity is a substrate-misassigned automated annotation and should be replaced by GO:0050527. [file:PSEPK/phaZ/phaZ-uniprot.txt, "SubName: Full=Poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) depolymerase"; AmiGO GO:0050527, "poly(3-hydroxyoctanoate) depolymerase activity"; https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0050527]
- GO:0046503 glycerolipid catabolic process is misleading because intracellular PHA mobilization is not glycerolipid catabolism; GO:0042620 poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) metabolic process is closer, but GO currently lacks a direct poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) catabolic process term for intracellular PHA mobilization. [AmiGO term graph, "GO:0042620 poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) metabolic process"; JBC 2007 PDF; https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0008152; https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/ae3e/1d24baa56e7222a02f12b2b3b75ee84cee02.pdf]


## 2026-11-07 comparative source audit

Completed all existing annotations for phaZ; preserved ordered source payloads and provider artifacts. Genuine existing provider reports were read as leads, with primary evidence and exact strain boundaries prioritized. Evidence, ontology snapshots, PAINT limits and supplementary provenance are under analysis/module_audits/bacterial_mcl_pha_synthesis_and_mobilization/psepk-consultation/. No new GO row added. PAINT target-leaf unavailable is not evidence of absence of evolutionary loss.

Full17170116 distinguishes KT2442 recombinant/native-granule assays from KT2440. Weak overnight tributyrin hydrolysis is retained as peripheral MF; native glycerolipid-catabolic flux is not inferred. The historical granule NEW/IDA proposal is retired in place with root authorization for unsupported target-direct provenance, not rejection of localization. Original row archived in retired-phaZ-proposal.yaml. Core location remains qualified, corroborated by native fraction detection without selective-enrichment claim. Native31468725 found no titre/yield improvement after phaZ deletion under its tested accumulation conditions, superseding unconditional older notes.

GO0004806 changed to MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED under the measured-activity/relevance-unknown enzyme-specificity tier. Positive overnight KT2442 tributyrin chemistry is retained. Full PMID17170116 Fig6 directly resolves HO monomer/dimer products from HO-rich copolymer, now stated with strain and copolymer limitations in core evidence. The proposed broader depolymerase has GO0016788 as immediate genus. Historical NEW granule row remains unchanged and retired.

# PAO1 PhaG evidence scope, 2026-11-07

The normal seed and raw files were retained. Actual Falcon attempt failed403; no provider report was fabricated. Cached PMID10713430 is abstract-only; publisher full-text attempts were inaccessible. Its abstract explicitly reports native P. aeruginosa phaG replacement and heterologous complementation of a P. putida phaG mutant. Native gluconate-supported PHA falls to approximately40% of wild type, whereas fatty-acid-supported accumulation remains at wild-type levels. This is conditional pathway contribution, not sole-route necessity or isolated protein kinetics.

Official AF209711/AAF61903.1 is 300/300 identical to Q51553 and records ATCC15692, a PAO1 strain alias. This identity proof is independently captured in ../literature-consultation/identity/results.json and AF209711.embl. P. putida complementation is a different host assay. The primary abstract says the data suggest transacylase activity; it does not claim a PAO1 purified forward-transfer assay. Curated UniProt FUNCTION plus P. putida reverse-transfer biochemistry support the acyltransferase inference, while 2022 heterologous E. coli controls favor transacylation over exclusively hydrolytic release.

Both original IBA rows descend from actual PTN002455972, seeded by BioH P13001, with PAO1 leaf PTN002251180 in SF5. The retrieved lineage has no recorded IRD/IKR, but that does not prove biochemical equivalence. The node includes PhaG and RhlA as well as BioH. No PAO1 pimelyl-ACP methyl-ester assay or biotin-specific physiological test was identified. Alternate PHA physiology alone cannot establish absence of secondary chemistry; retain UNDECIDED rather than claim a proven evolutionary loss.

The sole new assertion is inferred non-amino-acyl transfer, a molecular role not represented by either BioH seed row. It rests on target sequence-linked genetics, curated function and characterized PhaG biochemistry, not a need to satisfy module coverage. No new BP, location, DNA-regulatory or stress-response row is proposed. The PHA process is captured in core synthesis because PhaG supplies the hydroxyacyl reaction connecting monomer pools, not merely because its knockout changes output. RhlA and BioH share the broad fold but distinct reaction specificity, so no family-wide PhaG grant is implied.


## PR6194 follow-up — 2026-11-07

New normally fetched PMID36689471 directly establishes dedicated native PAO1 BioH/PA0502 and biotin rescue/complementation. GO0009102 is now MAOA because the ancestral pathway assignment exceeds PhaG evidence; GO0090499 remains UNDECIDED, as endogenous failure to compensate is not a purified PhaG-negative assay. Original authored NEW IC payload is unchanged. Frozen UniProt EC2.4.1.- versus hydroxyacyl-transfer chemistry is recorded as a source defect without rewriting the raw record.
